title: Eli Wilner August Frame Funding Program
summary: Eli Wilner & Company has announced that approximately $100,000 remains available through its museum grant program to support reframing and frame restoration projects at museums and cultural institutions nationwide. Funding partners committed $200,000 for the August 2026 funding cycle. Approximately half of those funds have already been awarded, with the remaining $100,000 available on a first-come, first-served basis through August 31, 2026, or until the funds are fully committed. The grants are intended to offset a portion of the cost of qualifying frame restoration and reframing projects. Recipient institutions are required to participate in the cost of the project, while grant funding covers the remaining approved portion. This shared-cost approach enables museums to undertake important projects that might otherwise be postponed due to budget limitations.

title: Georgetown University Art Galleries to host Rafael Lozano-Hemmer exhibition
summary: The Georgetown University Art Galleries announced Rafael Lozano-Hemmer: Look Alive, an exhibition of select installations by internationally acclaimed Mexican-Canadian artist Rafael Lozano-Hemmer, opening September 18, 2026. Presented across the Maria & Alberto de la Cruz Art Gallery and Lucille M. & Richard F. X. Spagnuolo Gallery, the exhibition brings together three works spanning more than three decades of the artist’s practice and explores the intersections of technology, participation, presence, and the act of looking. At the center of the exhibition is the premiere of Pulse Map, a site-specific installation created for Georgetown’s Maria & Alberto de la Cruz Gallery and the newest work in Lozano-Hemmer’s celebrated Pulse series. title: Akron Art Museum's historic 1899 building reopens September 23 following $12.5 million transformation
summary: The Akron Art Museum will reopen its historic 1899 Building to the public on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, following a $12.5 million transformation that dramatically expands the building’s public space and creates new opportunities for visitors to experience art, learn, create, and gather. The renovated historic building will be formally named the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation Building, recognizing the Foundation’s longstanding investment in the Museum and its future. Construction began in July 2025 and represents one of the most significant transformations of the Museum’s downtown campus since its 2007 expansion. title: Academy Museum announces 2026 Gala honorees: John Carpenter, Colman Domingo, and Charlize Theron
summary: The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures today announced filmmaker and composer John Carpenter, two-time Oscar®-nominated actor Colman Domingo, and Oscar®-winning actress Charlize Theron as the honorees of its annual fundraising gala on October 17, 2026. Theron will be honored with the Icon Award, Carpenter will receive the Luminary Award, and Domingo will be presented with the Vantage Award. The Academy Museum Gala advances the museum's mission to celebrate and preserve cinema. Through the generosity of gala donors, proceeds from the evening will help ensure the museum continues to present world-class exhibitions, support educational opportunities, offer dynamic public screenings, and remain accessible to visitors of all ages. Gala honorees directly champion the museum's mission by participating in public programming around the event. title: University Museums debuts five new exhibitions for fall 2026
summary: As more than 30,000 students return to Iowa State University’s campus this fall, University Museums is ready to welcome them with five new exhibitions spread across its two campus art museums and historic house museum. University Museums staff have been hard at work over the summer months making final preparations for the exhibitions – some years in the making – and organizing related student tours, class visits, special events and educational programs. “At their core, our museums are a trusted educational and cultural resource for ISU students, faculty and staff,” said David Schmitz, Warren and Beverly Madden Endowed Director and Chief Curator. “Our staff takes this mission to heart, being very responsive to how instructors teach while also creative with how we invite students and our broader community to experience art across campus.” Iowa State students, faculty, staff, and community members can

title: University of South Florida's Graphicstudio to present Jim Dine survey
summary: From September 8 through December 18, Graphicstudio, the University of South Florida’s world-renowned print studio, presents Jim Dine: Swaying in the Florida Night, a survey of the artist’s collaborative prints and sculpture editions created at the studio from 1973 to 1989. Jim Dine (b. 1935, Cincinnati, OH) is a multimedia artist whose practice encompasses painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, photography, poetry, and performance. The artworks on view offer an intimate look at the collaborative process of an artist who has consistently used printmaking as a platform for experimentation and creative expression. The exhibition features many of the symbolic motifs that Dine has employed throughout his artistic career, including bathrobes, skulls, hearts, and classical sculpture. summary: Galerie Barbara Thumm will present the eighth solo exhibition by Fiona Banner aka The Vanity Press, a founding member of the gallery. Fiona Banner aka The Vanity Press explores gender, language, and conflict through a range of media, including drawing, sculpture, performance and the moving image. She considers the meaning of the body politic and the politics of the body through a playful questioning of language. The exhibition is entered through a work The channel. title: Towner appoints Martin Clark as new CEO & Director
summary: Towner will welcome Martin Clark as CEO & Director in January 2027, following the departure of Joe Hill in spring 2026. Clark has been appointed by a panel led by Stephen Welton CBE, Chair of Towner’s Board of Trustees and Chair of British Business Bank with President of the Board David Dimbleby. Martin Clark, who previously worked with Towner as a member of the Turner Prize 2023 jury, joins the team after nearly a decade as Director of Camden Art Centre, London. During his tenure, he has grown the organisation’s profile and visibility, both nationally and internationally. He has also programmed and curated an internationally acclaimed series of exhibitions with artists including Mohammed Sami, Amy Sillman, Christodoulos Panayiotou, Martin Wong, Allison Katz, Lonnie Holley, Jesse Darling, Forrest Bess, Richard Wright, Nicola L., and the influential group exhibition, The Botanical Mind. title: Nivaagaard Collection to mark 150th anniversary of Christine Swane
summary: The Nivaagaard Collection will mark the 150th anniversary of Christine Swane’s birth with the most extensive presentation to date of the Danish artist’s wide-ranging career. Opening September 26, 2026, Christine Swane. A Multifaceted Individualist brings together paintings, ceramics and textiles to trace an artistic life that developed over seven decades. The exhibition follows Swane from her early years among the Funen Painters to the increasingly independent and experimental practice she established later in life. Swane (1876–1960) began as a painter, but her interests eventually expanded into ceramics, textiles and, late in her career, monumental mosaic. Across these different media, she maintained a distinctive sensitivity to color and a close engagement with the places and objects around her. title: Elvira Dyangani Ose appointed Artistic Director of Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa
summary: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa announced that internationally respected museum leader and curator Elvira Dyangani Ose will join the Museum as its Artistic Director, effective from October 1, 2026. Dyangani Ose’s career spans leading institutions across Europe, Africa, and the United States. She has served as Director of Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona (MACBA) and The Showroom London and previously held curatorial roles at Tate Modern in London and Creative Time in New York. She is currently the Artistic Director of the second Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial (2026–2027). Combining a Pan-African outlook with exceptional international experience, she is recognised for her artistic vision, institution building, collaborative leadership, and longstanding commitment to artists from Africa and its diaspora. title: Stephan Melzl explores chess and form in new exhibition at Thomas Rehbein Galerie
summary: Stephan Melzl explores the shifting relationships between bodies, objects and space in Guter Hoffnung, an exhibition of new paintings on view from September 4 through October 24, 2026. Across the works, familiar objects take on unexpected physical and psychological weight. Rounded vases echo the forms of women’s bodies, oversized boxing gloves appear almost protective, and chess pieces become metaphors for figures whose meaning changes according to their position in relation to everything around them. The idea of chess runs throughout the exhibition. Several paintings take their titles from the game, including Zugzwang, the term for a position in which a player is forced to move even though every available move may leave them worse off. title: Gazelli Art House to open new gallery space in New York's Chelsea
summary: This September, Gazelli Art House opens its new gallery in New York’s Chelsea Arts District with Put the Kettle On, an inaugural exhibition uniting eleven artists across more than six decades. Opening during Armory Week, the show draws unexpected connections between historical and contemporary practice — from post-war painting and sculpture to pioneering computer art and today’s AI and digital work — marking an exciting new chapter for the gallery across London, Baku and New York. Featuring works by Agil Abdullayev, Memo Akten, Derek Boshier, Pauline Boty, Harold Cohen, Brendan Dawes, Jake Elwes, Lilly Fenichel, Jann Haworth, Kalliopi Lemos, and Recycle Group. Mila Askarova, Founder & CEO of Gazelli Art House, said: “New York felt like the natural next step for us. title: San Francisco Arts Commission unveils thirteen new permanent public works of art
summary: The San Francisco Arts Commission, in collaboration with the San Francisco Recreation and Park Department, announced the unveiling of Gene Friend Recreation Center’s public art program following today’s community ribbon-cutting celebration attended by Mayor Daniel Lurie, city leaders, artists, and SoMa community members. The recreation center’s public art program contains 13 permanent works of art, including 12 purchased two-dimensional artworks on display along the building’s interior corridors and one commissioned, large-scale, and architecturally integrated artwork located in the gymnasium that honors well-known local leaders, veterans, elders, immigrants, and youth. “Public art helps make our civic spaces more welcoming, beautiful, and meaningful, particularly when those works reflect the people,

title: Romina Chuls reinterprets ancient Nasca textile in new installation
summary: A.I.R. Gallery will present La Cosecha (The Harvest), a textile and ceramic installation by 2025-2026 A.I.R. Fellow Romina Chuls. This is Chuls’ first solo exhibition in New York City. A pre-Hispanic funerary cloak poses an unanswered question. A hand holding an unidentified plant, three figures characterized as women, repeated supernatural faces, a multi-species crowd sticking out their tongues, and bean-like shapes are among the imagery that remain a mystery to this day. La Cosecha is a playful interpretation of the iconography of a Nasca textile dated 100-300 C.E., found in the Peruvian coastal desert and currently located in the collection of the Brooklyn Museum. title: Paulo Branco, Martin Scorsese, and Brigitte Bardot lead Cinemateca Portuguesa season
summary: Cinemateca Portuguesa’s rentrée opens — and continues — with a strong focus on notable figures from international cinema. From directors (Martin Scorsese, Noémia Delgado, Margaret Tait, Lino Brocka, Rita Azevedo Gomes, Frank Borzage, Hiroshi Shimizu) to actresses (Brigitte Bardot) and film producers (Paulo Branco), these featured and celebrated figures all share a defining role carved out by their works. In September, Cinemateca launches one of its major film cycles of 2026—likely one of the largest ever held at the institution—which will extend over the coming years. We are referring to a cycle dedicated to one of the most influential figures in Portuguese cinema in recent decades: Paulo Branco, an indelible name in Portuguese film. title: Otoh Collection returns with part VIII in Heritage's ANA Physical Cryptocurrency auction
summary: The Inaugural Example of Kialara’s “FOMO” Conceptual Post-it® Art Note will lead Heritage’s ANA Physical Cryptocurrency featuring The Otoh Collection, Part VIII World Coins Platinum Session and Signature® Auction September 3, an event in which 95 lots will cross the auction block as part of the eighth installment of the Otoh (“On the Other Hand”) Collection. The collection was first offered at Heritage in October 2023, and the September event will continue from its most recent auction in April 2026. “Physical cryptocurrency has developed into an increasingly established collecting category due to the broader evolution of digital currency and its ability to give individuals greater control over how assets are received, held and transferred,” says Cris Bierrenbach, Executive Vice President of International Numismatics at Heritage Auctions.

title: Howie Tsui and Crystal Mowry win prestigious 2026 Hnatyshyn Foundation awards
summary: The Hnatyshyn Foundation announces today that Howie Tsui (Vancouver) has received the Hnatyshyn Foundation Mid-Career Award for Excellence in Visual Arts and Crystal Mowry (Regina) has received the Hnatyshyn Foundation Mid-Career Award for Curatorial Excellence, prestigious peer-recognitions of excellence in the visual arts. Both have previously been shortlisted for the award. Valued respectively at $30,000 and $20,000 and awarded annually since 2006, the awards recognize excellence, innovation, and promise of outstanding artistic or curatorial achievement in the years ahead. Former laureates include Abbas Akhavan, Wanda Nanibush, Michelle Jacques, Heather Igloliorte, Kent Monkman, Rebecca Belmore, and more. title: Powerhouse Arts to present Masterpieces: A Virtual Experience of the Museo del Prado
summary: Powerhouse Arts announces the New York premiere of Masterpieces: A Virtual Experience of the Museo del Prado, an immersive virtual reality exhibition developed by ACCIONA Cultura in exclusive collaboration with Madrid's Museo Nacional del Prado. Running from October 1 through December 20, the experience invites visitors into a multi-sensory reimagining of one of the world's greatest museums, including fantastical, in-depth explorations of the museum's most celebrated, and rarely traveled, masterpieces. Billed as the first multi-user, location-based VR experience produced in collaboration with the Museo del Prado, Masterpieces does not attempt to recreate the Prado's galleries through the eyes of a curator or scholar; instead, it reenvisions the museum and its masterworks through the voice of a security guard on his final

title: Transmitter to present James Parker Foley solo exhibition Point of No Return
summary: Transmitter will present Point of No Return, a solo exhibition by James Parker Foley. Made across a period of profound personal transformation, this exhibition brings together two bodies of drawings; a group of graphite images begun during a residency in Mississippi in October 2022, and a subsequent body of colored pencil works begun in October 2023. The first body of drawings emerged while the artist was privately grappling with a desire to live as a gay man. This secret desire became the narrative undercurrent for a hidden fantasy world, drawn on intimately-scaled paper in the vulnerable medium of graphite. The colored pencil works that followed a year later, after the artist had begun to transition, wrestle with what it means to be a man, and how to build a life for himself as a trans person. title: Springfield Art Museum Foundation welcomes Erin Lawrence and Andy Drennen to Board of Directors
summary: The Springfield Art Museum Foundation has announced the appointment of Erin Lawrence and Andy Drennen, CFP®, to its Board of Directors, adding two accomplished community leaders whose expertise, relationships, and commitment to Springfield will help advance the Foundation’s mission and support the transformational renovation and expansion of the Springfield Art Museum. The appointments come at an important moment for the Foundation and the Museum as work continues on the Museum’s ambitious capital project. Through the 2028 Campaign, the Foundation has led the private fundraising effort supporting the Museum’s renovation and expansion, bringing the campaign to over $71 million raised toward creating a significantly expanded and revitalized Museum for the community and region. title: Estorick Collection to highlight Italian photography pioneers Wanda and Marion Wulz
summary: This September, the Estorick Collection presents a major exhibition exploring the pioneering work of sisters Wanda Wulz (1903–1984) and Marion Wulz (1905–1993), key figures in the development of avant-garde photography in 20th-century Italy. Organised in collaboration with the Fondazione Alinari per la Fotografia and with the support of Calliope Arts Foundation, the show also traces the wider legacy of the Wulz family, whose photographic practice spanned generations. In 1928, Wanda and Marion inherited the photography studio founded by their grandfather, Giuseppe Wulz, and later run by their father, Carlo. Having been immersed in photography from an early age, the sisters transformed the studio into a vibrant centre of artistic and commercial production in their native Trieste.
